description: A single-panel flowchart with no axes, scale bars or plotted data, describing a machine-learning (ML) design framework for low-density Fe–Mn–Al–C austenitic steels. At the left, a blue box "Possible candidates" feeds a large purple dashed region labelled "Filter". The Filter is bounded below by the blue bar "Predicting models based on machine-learning method" and on the right by the purple vertical bar "Empirical formula". Inside the Filter, candidates pass through five sequential decision diamonds: "κ exists?", "A single γ region?", "(γ+κ) region in 500-600°C?", "κ fraction high?", and "Low density?". Each diamond emits a green "Yes" arrow that continues the chain and a green upward "No" arrow that rejects the candidate. Exiting the Filter, a yellow arrow labelled "Experimental tests" enters the yellow diamond "Good properties?"; a "No" leaves upward through the purple "Feedback" arrow back to the predicting models, while "Yes" points left to the cyan "Success" box. The figure argues that ML screening of composition against κ/γ phase criteria plus empirical density rules narrows candidates before experimental validation, closing a feedback loop that iterates until good properties are achieved.

observations.observation: The flowchart begins with a blue box labelled 'Possible candidates' that provides the input compositions to the screening Filter.
The Filter stage contains five sequential decision diamonds, in order: 'κ exists?', 'A single γ region?', '(γ+κ) region in 500-600°C?', 'κ fraction high?' and 'Low density?'.
Each decision diamond emits a green 'Yes' arrow continuing the chain and a green upward 'No' arrow that rejects the candidate.
The Filter block is underlain by the blue bar reading 'Predicting models based on machine-learning method', identifying the ML models that drive the screening.
A purple vertical bar labelled 'Empirical formula' borders the right side of the Filter block, providing the density criterion of the 'Low density?' decision.
A yellow 'Experimental tests' arrow leads from the filtered candidates into the yellow 'Good properties?' decision diamond.
A 'No' result at 'Good properties?' returns upward via the purple 'Feedback' arrow to the predicting models, while a 'Yes' result leads left to the cyan 'Success' box.
The printed decision criterion '(γ+κ) region in 500-600°C' specifies a temperature window of 500-600 °C for the two-phase γ+κ region.
The caption states the figure is the framework of the design process of the low-density Fe–Mn–Al–C austenitic steels by machine learning.
The citing text states the design strategy is focused on establishing the correlation between the composition of low-density steel and its microstructure characteristics.
The citing text proposes a novel machine learning-based design strategy aimed at expediting development of low-density Fe–Mn–Al–C austenitic steels.

subfigures.description: The filter framework: a blue 'Possible candidates' box feeding a purple dashed 'Filter' block that contains five sequential decision diamonds ('κ exists?', 'A single γ region?', '(γ+κ) region in 500-600°C?', 'κ fraction high?', 'Low density?'), each with a green forward 'Yes' arrow and a green upward 'No' arrow. The block is underlain by the 'Predicting models based on machine-learning method' bar and bounded right by the 'Empirical formula' bar.

The experimental-validation and feedback loop: a yellow 'Experimental tests' arrow enters the 'Good properties?' diamond; 'No' feeds back upward via the purple 'Feedback' arrow toward the predicting models, and 'Yes' leads left to the cyan 'Success' box.
